clue.text: A little arch framing a lamp

indicators.note: framing means the first word's letters go round the second's like a frame

parts.note: arch in the sense of knowing or cunning, i.e. sly
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: A small decorative arch built around a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like a noun for a structure but is the adjective meaning roguish, SLY, which goes round LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, i.e. a little.

clue.text: Under a quarter lock, giving rise to anxiety

indicators.note: under means in this down clue the hair word is placed below the compass letter

parts.note: S for south, one of the four quarters of the compass
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Being locked up under a quarter breeds anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door or canal but is a lock of hair, TRESS, written under S in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental strain and worry.

clue.text: Dirty little rascal running water

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A grubby little rascal playing in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire; 'running water' is a cryptic way of saying river.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure means contaminated or unclean.

clue.text: Female beast or male, fire anyway

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: anyway means in any manner, so the letters of fire come in some other order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fire at any animal, male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' signals that FIRE is rearranged to IFER, which follows HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet calved.

clue.text: Appear late for public honour

parts.note: the late means the dead, shown publicly in their coffin as a mark of respect, while appear late suggests oversleeping

explanation.surface: Turning up late to receive a public award.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead dignitary's body displayed for public mourning is the honour described.

clue.text: Charge brought by copper in unusual case

indicators.note: in places the copper symbol inside the rearranged letters
unusual tells us the letters of case appear in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman brings a charge in an odd case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but here is the metal; CU goes inside ACSE, the rearrangement of CASE signalled by 'unusual'.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with an offence is to accuse them.

clue.text: Insurance for which one may conceal how old one is

parts.note: to conceal is to cover
one's age

explanation.surface: A policy under which people may hide their age.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy provides.

clue.text: French article about a certain issue making no sense

parts.note: un is the French for a or an
re means about or concerning
a son is a particular kind of issue, offspring

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece about a certain topic is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic but means offspring, so SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is irrationality, the absence of sense.

clue.text: Smooth variation of current towards the end of the day

parts.note: smooth means level or even
a tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea, a changing current

explanation.surface: A smooth change in the current near day's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening.

clue.text: Paid a visit and patched things up

definitions.meaning: to have ... to a place is to have gone there

explanation.surface: Someone dropped by and mended things.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair can mean go (to a place) as well as mend, so both senses fit the past tense.

clue.text: Reluctant as ever?

indicators.note: the question mark invites us to treat the two words as letters to be rearranged rather than read literally

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is as unwilling as they always were.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no word indicator: the question mark alone hints that AS EVER be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, unwilling to do something.

clue.text: Rank 23 with a social worker

parts.note: 23 refers to the clue whose answer is MATERIAL; serge is a material
an ant is a worker insect living in a social colony

explanation.surface: A rank held alongside a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the clue answered by a word for fabric, so take a fabric: SERGE, a twilled cloth. 'social worker' is a whimsical description of an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a military or police rank.

clue.text: Operated surrounded by pictures, being thorough

indicators.note: surrounded by means the operated word sits inside the pictures word

parts.note: pictures collectively are art
operated as a machine does, ran

explanation.surface: A thorough job run amid a gallery of pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter or out-and-out, thorough in a bad sense, as in an arrant fool.

clue.text: Arranged a deal, plainly affected by the squeeze

definitions.meaning: shrunk or made smaller by pressure

explanation.surface: A deal was agreed while the economy was being squeezed.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracted means agreed by contract and also shrunk.

clue.text: Good grip for use in defence

definitions.text: Good grip for use in defence

parts.words: Good grip for use in defence
parts.note: read as two words, a firm hold; as one, a fortified place used to defend

explanation.surface: A firm grip is useful when defending yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or castle is a defensive position, read here as a powerful clutch.

clue.text: A shopper maybe wanting more cuts

indicators.note: wanting, in the sense of deficient or out of order, shows the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper who wants more price cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MORE CUTS are rearranged; 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is someone who buys, of whom a shopper is one example.

clue.text: Thought the holy man about 51a visionary

parts.note: a thought is an idea
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
ST, short for saint

explanation.surface: A thoughtful holy man of about fifty-one is a dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues high principles, often impractically, like a dreamer.

clue.text: The — of the dooms we have imagined for the mighty dead." Keats (Endymion)

definitions.text: The — of the dooms we have imagined for the mighty dead." Keats (Endymion)

parts.words: The — of the dooms we have imagined for the mighty dead." Keats (Endymion)
parts.note: a line from Keats's long poem Endymion with one noun left out for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats's Endymion with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing noun in the line means magnificence or splendour.

clue.text: To tell less than the complete truth should be beneath the government

definitions.text: To tell less than the complete truth

parts.note: beneath means under
the state is the government of a country

explanation.surface: Lying by omission ought to be beneath any government.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to represent it as less than it really is.

clue.text: Name some judge or general

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Name any judge or general you like.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a common male first name.

clue.text: Superior accepting it is subject to limitations

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: superior quality is fine

explanation.surface: A superior who accepts that it has its limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with bounds or an end is limited.

clue.text: Clash about the trainee making off

indicators.note: about means the clash word is placed around the trainee letter

parts.note: a clash is a fight
L for learner, the trainee driver's plate

explanation.surface: A clash over a trainee who runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is the act of fleeing or escaping.

clue.text: Aims for travel perhaps

definitions.meaning: a gun is trained on a target
railway vehicles, one way to travel

explanation.surface: Someone sets goals, for travel perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains is a verb for pointing a weapon and a noun for railway rolling stock.

clue.text: Relevant data

definitions.meaning: information used in writing or research

explanation.surface: Facts that matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means pertinent (a material fact) and also information gathered for a book or report.

clue.text: A girl assistant retained by guys

indicators.note: retained by means the helper word is held inside the guys word

parts.note: guys are men
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A girl helper kept on by the men.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Five looking around will be in want of food

indicators.note: around means the looking word goes round the numeral

parts.note: looking hard is staring
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people peering about are hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Starving means suffering from hunger, badly needing to eat.

clue.text: Certain military personnel go-and come back

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a go or a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Some soldiers go off and later come home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a corps of the British Army. 'go' is the noun, as in 'your go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to come back to a place.

clue.text: He daren't appear to be a supporter

indicators.note: appear to be signals the letters merely seem to form a new word when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man too timid to be seen backing a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HE DARENT are rearranged, signalled loosely by 'appear to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause or person.
